correctness.rationale: Independent rate-p_i Poisson processes realize exactly the original discrete mark sequence. Given last first-arrival time t and type j, other counts are independent zero-truncated Poissons; their means a_i and singleton probabilities q_i yield negative conditional covariance. Last-type weights are q_i/Q; mixing adds a nonpositive covariance because a_i increase and q_i decrease with p_i. The singleton conditional mean strictly decreases in t, while the total count conditional mean strictly increases; the total covariance identity gives strict negativity for all m>=2 and p_i>0. Reconstructed boundaries m=1 and p_i=0 excluded; 59 exact-rational finite-state comparisons passed, but finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Uniform case covered by Myers–Wilf 2003 complete joint distribution; not claimed new. Brown–Peköz–Ross 2008 gives nonuniform marginal terminal counts and cover-time distributions, not their mixed covariance. Anceaume et al. 2014 and Zoroa et al. 2016 cover nonuniform marginal and fixed-time behavior. The new universal negative covariance under arbitrary unequal p and its conditional structural proof were not subsumed by inspected statements. Residual risk of an earlier broad nonuniform joint-law theorem remains.
residual_risks: A broader pre-existing arbitrary-probability joint stopping-time/terminal-singleton theorem may imply the sign; not found in inspected sources.

value.rationale: Nonuniform coupon collection is motivated by heterogeneous species detection and coverage testing. The theorem resolves a dependence-sign question between collection effort and how many types remain unique at first complete coverage for the entire positive simplex, independent of heterogeneity. Separate marginals and monotonic cover-time results cannot determine this sign, and the proof identifies a structural conditional-order mechanism. No downstream publication-size consequence or numeric sharp bound is asserted.
